Chandni Chowk was laid out around 1650 as the main street of Shahjahanabad, the city Shah Jahan built beside the Red Fort. Walk it with a historian or archaeologist from the Red Fort end to Fatehpuri Masjid and read the street as a document: places of worship of several faiths along one road, bazaars that still keep their trades, and the havelis, katras and lanes behind the frontage.

The date, start time, pace and language are arranged to suit your group.

What it covers

  • One street, several faiths: the Digambar Jain Lal Mandir, the Gauri Shankar temple, Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib and the Sunehri Masjid
  • Dariba Kalan, Kinari Bazaar and the spice market of Khari Baoli
  • Havelis and katras behind the main street
  • Fatehpuri Masjid at the western end of the street

How the time is spent

  1. The Red Fort end 15 min

    How Shahjahanabad was planned around the fort and its main street.

  2. One street, several faiths 35 min

    The Lal Mandir, the Gauri Shankar temple, Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib and the Sunehri Masjid, visited respectfully and only where visitors are welcome.

    You: date each building from its details

  3. The bazaars 40 min

    Dariba Kalan, Kinari Bazaar and Khari Baoli: how a trade keeps its lane for generations.

    You: map who sells what

  4. Havelis and katras 25 min

    The houses and courtyard markets behind the main street, and what has happened to them.

  5. Fatehpuri Masjid 20 min

    The mosque that closes the street at its western end.

  6. Wrap-up 10 min

    Your questions, and where to eat or shop before you leave.

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Read Chandni Chowk as the planned main street of Shahjahanabad.
  • Recognise how places of worship, bazaars and houses shared one street.
  • Distinguish the Mughal-period fabric from later rebuilding along the street.

You take away

A street map of the buildings you saw, with their dates.

Where
Chandni Chowk, Old Delhi
For
Schools, colleges, companies and the public
Length
2 to 2.5 hours
When
Monday to Saturday, when the bazaars are open; most shops in the main market are shut on Sundays. Mornings are best.
Led by
A historian or archaeologist who specialises in Delhi's buildings
Language
English, Hindi or both. Other languages on request, through our partners.
Group size
Agreed with you. Smaller and larger groups are welcome.
Meeting point
Agreed with you, near Chandni Chowk metro station or the Red Fort end of the street.
What to bring
Comfortable shoes and a small bag worn in front. The lanes are narrow and crowded. Shoes come off and heads are covered where a place of worship asks.
Entry fees
None of the places on the walk charges an entry fee.
Price
₹1,800 per person for 2, ₹900 each for 10 or more, including GST
